lang-rust.message: After shutdown, deregister_source returns Ok without calling registry.deregister. On current_thread the mio Poll is not dropped until the Runtime itself is dropped (shutdown2 returns the core, which keeps core.driver). So the fd stays registered in the epoll/kqueue set with a token that points at a ScheduledIo which can now be freed when the Registration is dropped. This is sound only because nothing polls the Poll after shutdown, and that is a convention rather than something the types enforce. Any later poll or dispatch of that Poll would dereference freed memory. Making the invariant structural is safer: drop the driver in current_thread shutdown2 as well, which also closes the fds at shutdown as the PR intends.

shutdown2 calls driver.shutdown but keeps core.driver alive, so the mio Poll (epoll/kqueue fd) survives until the Runtime is dropped. This contradicts the PR's goal of releasing the fds at shutdown, and it is the reason the stale-registration concern above exists. Taking the driver here, after shutdown and before release_io, closes the Poll at shutdown too.

park_timeout (and the same pattern in park at line 148) calls expect("driver missing") in non-test code. The driver is taken only in Inner::shutdown, which runs after every worker has stopped parking (shutdown_core waits for all cores). So this is unreachable today, but a panic on a worker thread would be a hard failure if that ordering ever changes. Treating None as 'no driver, use the condvar' would degrade gracefully.

The else branch of Inner::shutdown used to skip silently when the lock was contended. It is now debug_assert!(false), so debug and test builds panic on contention. In release builds the driver is still not dropped and its fds stay open, which is exactly the leak this PR removes. The invariant (no core is parking once shutdown_core runs) makes contention unreachable, so the assert documents that. Consider keeping an explicit comment on the invariant, or returning early with a log instead of a debug-only panic.

pragmatist.message: The `else { debug_assert!(false, ...) }` branch only fires in debug builds, and in release a locked driver silently skips the release, so the fd leak this PR fixes comes back unnoticed. It also conflicts with the PR's own 'not covered: shutdown_background with a worker that never exits' case. Either drop the branch or document why the lock can never be held here.

skeptic.message: If try_lock fails at shutdown, release builds silently skip both driver.shutdown and release_io, so the fds leak again and registrations are never shut down (tasks waiting on I/O would hang). Previously a failed try_lock also skipped driver.shutdown, so this is not a regression, but the new debug_assert only covers debug builds. Consider falling back to a blocking lock, which is safe since all cores have stopped parking.

The test only runs on Linux and uses a combined threshold, so a leak of at most 2 fds across 50 runtimes would pass. It also does not cover the new behavior changes (signal()/ctrl_c() through a dropped multi_thread handle returning an error, register after shutdown returning the shutdown error). Tests for those would pin the documented behavior change.

dropped.message: Deregister after shutdown leaves the fd registered with a dangling token while the current_thread Poll is still alive.
debug_assert!(false) branch silently skips release in release builds.
expect("driver missing") in park_timeout/park could panic a worker if shutdown ordering changes.
Test threshold too loose and behavior changes (signal after drop) are untested.

findings.message: If `try_lock` fails in `Inner::shutdown`, release builds skip both `driver.shutdown` and `release_io`, so the driver's fds stay open (the leak this PR fixes) and registrations are not shut down, with no signal at all. `debug_assert!(false, ...)` only catches this in debug/test builds. Previously the contended case was also skipped silently, so this is not a regression. The invariant that no core is parking once shutdown runs makes it unreachable today, but the release-build behaviour should be stated explicitly. Either write the invariant down in a comment next to the branch, or make the fallback still call `handle.release_io()` (or retry the lock) so the resources are released even if the invariant is ever broken.

`shutdown2` shuts the driver down but keeps it in `core.driver`, so on current_thread the mio `Poll` lives until the `Runtime` itself is dropped. Meanwhile, `deregister_source` after shutdown now returns `Ok` without calling `registry.deregister`, and `RegistrationSet::shutdown` has already released the set's `Arc`s. That means a source can stay in the epoll/kqueue set with a token pointing at a `ScheduledIo` that gets freed once its `Registration` drops. Today this is sound only because nothing polls the driver between `shutdown2` and the drop of the `Runtime`. That is a convention, not something the types enforce. Taking the driver out here, as multi_thread now does, would make the guarantee structural and close the `Poll` at shutdown too.
